blind.B1: Yes. PoWeR (progressive weighted wheel running) vs sedentary, gastrocnemius, BALB/c mice, with PBS or C26 tumour; all 22 sequenced samples carry the exercise factor (11 SED, 11 PoWeR). Locators: S2.7.p1, S3.7.p1.
blind.B2: S3.7.p1: PBS PoWeR vs PBS SED (42 DEGs), C26 SED vs PBS SED (2740), C26 PoWeR vs C26 SED (963); n = 2-3 per sex per group, sexes collapsed (S2.8.p1); GEO cells 6/6/5/5.
blind.B3: No repeated measures: one gastrocnemius per mouse, single time point at endpoint. Library names P1..P24 are unique; no pairing key needed (packet A keys link 0/22).
blind.B4: The paper does not say (S2.7.p1 only says normalization and statistical comparisons with DESeq2, in Partek Flow); pairwise comparisons are reported.
blind.B5: S2.7.p1: 'Genes with a false discovery rate (Benjamini-Hochberg method) adjusted P-value <0.05 were identified as differentially expressed genes'; genes with geometric average <1 over all samples excluded before correction; no fold-change cutoff. Counts: 42 / 2740 / 963 (S3.7.p1).

checks.evidence: All 22 samples have the SED/PoWeR factor; analyzed (S3.7.p1, packet A grouping columns).
grp = PBS_SED 6, PBS_PoWeR 6, C26_SED 5, C26_PoWeR 5 equals FIG8 legend n; no exclusions; matrix labels agree with GEO titles.
Treatment = PoWeR, control = SED within each tumour arm; tumour contrast C26 vs PBS; matches S3.7.p1 ordering.
Independent mice, one muscle each (S2.2, S2.7.p1); record states repeated_measure_unit none; packet A keys do not link samples.

Paper silent on joint vs pairwise fit. Joint ~0+cell fit used; counts differ a lot from paper (0 vs 42, 255 vs 963, 2165 vs 2740) but only the joint fit is reported. Main cause is likely the normalized-count/limma deviation, not the joint model.
checks.fix: Optionally add a pairwise-only limma fit (each pair of groups alone) as a sensitivity to show the joint model is not driving the count gap.

checks.evidence: Batch=1 and sex crossed with grp (recorded). Housing is not recorded: sedentary mice were group housed while wheel-running mice are presumably singly housed (S2.8.p1 notes food could not be measured in group-housed sedentary mice; GEO treatment_protocol 'sedentary in group housing'); housing is aliased with the exercise factor. Also samples were picked to represent group averages (S2.7.p1), recorded in reconstruction.
checks.fix: Add a confounding note that housing is inherent to the exercise factor and cannot be separated.

checks.evidence: File is DESeq2 median-ratio normalized counts (integer fraction 0.03); limma on log2(x+1) is the declared deviation; frac_p_gt_0.9 0.056-0.11, no pile-up near 1.

BH FDR < 0.05, no fold-change cutoff, strict inequality, transcribed exactly from S2.7.p1. The mechanical flag other_rule_matches_paper is not convincing: closest rule gives 889 vs paper 963 and no rule reproduces 42 or 2740, so the gap reflects the data/method deviation, not another threshold.

Same three contrasts compared at the same rule (HANDBACK table). Counts disagree and this is shown openly; the count gap is not listed in the recorded discrepancy JSON (only matrix input and orientation are).
checks.fix: Optionally add the DEG-count gap and its likely cause (no raw counts, no Partek geometric-mean filter) to the discrepancy list.

checks.evidence: No stop or refusal; ORA for PBS PoWeR vs PBS SED did not run because there were 0 DEGs, a true and sufficient reason.

human_items: Joint versus pairwise fits when the paper is silent: only the joint fit is reported while counts differ a lot from the paper.
Whether to report the paper's DEG rule when its counts are not reproduced (0 vs 42 for healthy exercise effect); here the stated rule was applied and the gap is shown in HANDBACK.
summary: 该案例的分组、对比方向、阈值(BH FDR<0.05、无倍数变化限制)和重复测量判断均与论文一致,没有发现阻断性或主要问题。只有归一化计数的 limma 路线是已声明的偏离,DEG 数量与论文差距较大(0 对 42,255 对 963),建议补充成对拟合的敏感性分析并在差异清单中记录该差距,另有圈养条件与运动因素混杂未记录。总体判定为通过。
